report.headline: Routine surveillance
report.patient_summary: No features of active ulceration were detected in this scan. Continue checking your feet every day, moisturise dry skin (avoiding between the toes), and keep up your regular diabetes reviews.
report.clinical_assessment: Automated analysis returns a fused ulceration risk of 28.0% (LOW). The convolutional classifier assigned P(ulcer) = 1.5% to the plantar image (temperature-calibrated, T = 1.00); clinical covariates applied a +2.00 log-odds adjustment. Clinical history contributes a net +2.00 log-odds, raising the image-derived probability of 0.015 to a fused risk of 0.280. Ranked by influence: Peripheral Neuropathy (1, OR 2.36); Diabetes Duration (22 years, OR 1.58); Patient Age (81 years, OR 1.38); Body Mass Index (17.2 kg/m², OR 1.25). The aggregate clinical shift was capped at the configured limit so that history cannot override the imaging finding. IWGDF stratification places this patient in category 1 (Moderate risk) on the basis of: loss of protective sensation or peripheral arterial disease.
report.visual_analysis: Grad-CAM++ attribution for the ulcer class shows one broad region of activation spanning 57.3% of the field, peaking lower-central. Peak activation 1.00, mean 0.55, spatial focality 0.43 (1.0 = single tight hotspot). The classifier assigned P(ulcer) = 0.015 to this image.
report.triage:
1. Continue routine diabetic foot screening at the guideline interval
2. Reinforce daily self-inspection, including between the toes
3. Confirm footwear fit and check for pressure points
4. Re-image promptly if any new lesion, colour change or swelling appears
5. IWGDF risk category 1 (Moderate risk) - recommended screening interval: Every 6-12 months

report.limitations: Single-image analysis of a cropped plantar patch. The model was trained on 224x224 tissue patches and has not been validated on whole-foot photographs, on skin tones outside the training distribution, or against histopathology. Clinical coefficients are literature-informed priors, not fitted to outcomes in this cohort. Wound depth, infection and ischaemia are not assessed.
